gloss: by accident; in a state; the most
title: ter-
pattern: ter- + root: tertinggal, tersesat (by accident) · tertutup (a state) · terbesar (the most)
explanation: ter- describes something that happens without anyone meaning it to: tertinggal (left behind), terjatuh (fell over), tersesat (got lost). It also describes the state something is in, rather than an action someone did: Pintunya tertutup (the door is shut) beside Pintunya ditutup (the door was shut, by someone), and terjual habis (sold out). On a describing word it means the most, mainly in writing and on signs: terbesar (the biggest), terdekat (the nearest), termurah (the cheapest). A few ter- words are simply words now, listed as they are: terlambat (late), terkenal (famous), tertarik (interested).
natural: Explaining small mishaps without blaming anyone (Maaf, kuncinya tertinggal), reading signs and notices, and asking for the nearest anything: ATM terdekat di mana?
stiff: In casual speech ke- often replaces ter- for accidents: ketinggalan, kebawa (taken by mistake), and getting lost is nyasar: Aku tadi nyasar. For the most in conversation, paling is more usual than ter-: yang paling murah.

examples.english: Sorry I'm late, I got lost.

gap.why: Getting lost just happened, nobody did it to you, so ter-; disesatkan means someone misled you.

examples.english: I left my phone in the taxi.

gap.why: Left behind by accident is tertinggal; ditinggal sounds deliberate, and meninggal means to die.

examples.audioHint: Ha pe saya tertinggal di taksi.

gap.why: Sold out is a finished state, terjual habis; dijual means for sale.
The nearest is ter- + dekat; in conversation, yang paling dekat says the same.
